subject: maths
title: Year 5 Multiplying Fractions by Whole Numbers
seo_title: Year 5 Multiplying Fractions Worksheets: Fractions and Mixed Numbers × Whole Numbers (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Multiply proper fractions and mixed numbers by whole numbers, supported by materials and diagrams.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on multiplying fractions by whole numbers for the National Curriculum: bar models and repeated addition, mixed-number answers, fractions of amounts, mixed numbers × whole numbers and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Multiply the numerator by the whole number. Keep the denominator.
key_sub: 3 × 2/5 = 6/5 = 1 1/5, not 6/15. For a mixed number, multiply the wholes and the fraction: 2 1/4 × 3 = 6 + 3/4 = 6 3/4.
body_html:
The big idea

Multiplying a fraction by a whole number is repeated addition. 3 × 25 means 25 + 25 + 25.

Multiply the numerator by the whole number. Keep the denominator. The denominator tells you the size of the parts, and the size does not change.

CalculationThinkAnswer
4 × 154 parts that are each 1545
3 × 253 × 2 = 6 fifths65 = 1 15
5 × 345 × 3 = 15 quarters154 = 3 34

Answers bigger than 1

Change an improper fraction to a mixed number. Divide the numerator by the denominator. The answer is the number of wholes, and the remainder is the new numerator.

Example

6 × 34 = ?

6 × 3 = 18, so the answer is 184. 18 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 2, so it is 4 24. Simplify 24 to 12.

Answer: 4 12

Fractions of amounts

When you multiply a whole number by a fraction, × means “of”. Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator.

Mixed number × whole number

Partition the mixed number into wholes and a fraction. Multiply both parts, then add.

Example

1 25 × 4 = ?

1 × 4 = 4 and 25 × 4 = 85 = 1 35. Add: 4 + 1 35.

Answer: 5 35

You can also change the mixed number to an improper fraction first: 1 25 = 75, and 75 × 4 = 285 = 5 35.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3 × 25 = 615 (multiplying the denominator too)Keep the denominator: 65 = 1 15
3 × 25 = 3 25 (adding the whole number)3 × means 3 lots of 25
2 14 × 3 = 6 14 (multiplying only the whole number)Multiply the fraction too: 14 × 3 = 34, so 6 34
1 25 × 4 = 4 35 (losing the whole from 85)85 = 1 35, so add 1 more whole: 5 35
214 = 4 14 (a slip when dividing)21 ÷ 4 = 5 remainder 1, so 5 14

faq.q: What fractions do Year 5 children learn to multiply?
faq.a: In the National Curriculum, Year 5 pupils multiply proper fractions and mixed numbers by whole numbers, using diagrams to help. Multiplying two fractions together, such as 1/4 × 1/2, comes in Year 6.

faq.q: How do you multiply a fraction by a whole number?
faq.a: Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator. For example, 3 × 2/5 = 6/5, which is 1 1/5.

faq.q: How do you multiply a mixed number by a whole number?
faq.a: Multiply the whole number part and the fraction part separately, then add. For example, 2 1/4 × 3 = 6 + 3/4 = 6 3/4.

faq.q: How do you teach multiplying fractions in Year 5?
faq.a: Start with bar models and repeated addition, so 3 × 2/5 is 2/5 + 2/5 + 2/5 = 6/5. Then move on to the rule, changing improper fractions to mixed numbers, and word problems.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 3 bars with 25 shaded in each. What is 3 × 25?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 3 lots of 2 is 3 × 2 = 6. Each part is 15, so 3 × 25 = 65, which is 1 15. The parts are still the same size, so the denominator stays 5.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 4 bars with 13 shaded in each. What is 4 × 13?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 4 lots of 1 is 4 × 1 = 4. Each part is 13, so 4 × 13 = 43, which is 1 13. The parts are still the same size, so the denominator stays 3.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 5 bars with 14 shaded in each. What is 5 × 14?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 5 lots of 1 is 5 × 1 = 5. Each part is 14, so 5 × 14 = 54, which is 1 14. The parts are still quarters, so the denominator stays 4.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 3 bars with 47 shaded in each. What is 3 × 47?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 3 lots of 4 is 3 × 4 = 12. Each part is 17, so 3 × 47 = 127, which is 1 57. The parts are still the same size, so the denominator stays 7.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 3 bars with 38 shaded in each. What is 3 × 38?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 3 lots of 3 is 3 × 3 = 9. Each part is 18, so 3 × 38 = 98, which is 1 18. The parts are still the same size, so the denominator stays 8.

items.q: Each bar is 1 whole. There are 4 bars with 25 shaded in each. What is 4 × 25?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 4 lots of 2 is 4 × 2 = 8. Each part is 15, so 4 × 25 = 85, which is 1 35. The parts are still the same size, so the denominator stays 5.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 4 × 38?
c: 38 + 38 + 38 + 38
48 + 38
38 + 38 + 38
items.e: 4 × 38 means 4 lots of 38, so add 38 4 times: 38 + 38 + 38 + 38 = 128.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 3 × 29?
c: 29 + 29
39 + 29
29 + 29 + 29
items.e: 3 × 29 means 3 lots of 29, so add 29 3 times: 29 + 29 + 29 = 69.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 5 × 23?
c: 53 + 23
23 + 23 + 23 + 23
23 + 23 + 23 + 23 + 23
items.e: 5 × 23 means 5 lots of 23, so add 23 5 times: 23 + 23 + 23 + 23 + 23 = 103.

items.q: 29 + 29 + 29 + 29 = ?
items.e: Add the numerators and keep the denominator, because the parts are all ninths: 29 + 29 + 29 + 29 = 89. This is the same as 4 × 29. Do not add the denominators.

items.q: 18 + 18 + 18 + 18 + 18 = ?
items.e: Add the numerators and keep the denominator, because the parts are all eighths: 18 + 18 + 18 + 18 + 18 = 58. This is the same as 5 × 18. Do not add the denominators.

items.q: 310 + 310 + 310 = ?
items.e: Add the numerators and keep the denominator, because the parts are all tenths: 310 + 310 + 310 = 910. This is the same as 3 × 310. Do not add the denominators.

items.q: 3 × 27 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 3 × 2 = 6, so the answer is 67.

items.q: 15 × 4 = ?
items.e: 15 × 4 is the same as 4 × 15. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 4 × 1 = 4, so the answer is 45.

items.q: 2 × 49 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 2 × 4 = 8, so the answer is 89.

items.q: 110 × 7 = ?
items.e: 110 × 7 is the same as 7 × 110. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 7 × 1 = 7, so the answer is 710.

items.q: 5 × 15 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 5 × 1 = 5, so the answer is 55. 5 ÷ 5 = 1, so the answer is 1.

items.q: 23 × 3 = ?
items.e: 23 × 3 is the same as 3 × 23. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 3 × 2 = 6, so the answer is 63. 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so the answer is 2.

items.q: 4 × 34 = ?
items.e: Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 4 × 3 = 12, so the answer is 124. 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so the answer is 3.

items.q: 311 × 3 = ?
items.e: 311 × 3 is the same as 3 × 311. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 3 × 3 = 9, so the answer is 911.

items.e: The jumps end at 2 23. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 4 × 2 = 8, so the answer is 83. 8 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 2, so 83 = 2 23.

items.q: Which multiplication has an answer between 2 and 3?
items.e: 3 × 34 = 94 = 2 14, which is between 2 and 3. 4 × 15 = 45, 5 × 23 = 103 = 3 13 and 2 × 56 = 106 = 1 23.

items.q: ? × 35 = 2 25
items.e: Change 2 25 to an improper fraction: 2 × 5 + 2 = 12, so it is 125. The denominator stays 5, so ? × 3 = 12. 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Check: 4 × 35 = 125 = 2 25.

items.q: Ethan says 4 × 23 = 812. What mistake did he make?
c: He multiplied the denominator by 4 as well.
He forgot to change it to a mixed number.
items.e: 812 = 23, so Ethan did not change the size at all. Only the numerator is multiplied: 4 × 2 = 8, and the parts are still thirds. 4 × 23 = 83 = 2 23.

items.q: Oliver works out 7 × 34 = 214. Which mixed number is the same as 214?
items.e: 21 ÷ 4 = 5 remainder 1 (5 × 4 = 20). 5 wholes and 1 quarter left over: 214 = 5 14.

items.q: The whole bar is 12. Find 23 of 12.
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 4 = 8. So 23 of 12 = 8.

items.q: The whole bar is 20. 34 × 20 = ?
items.e: × means “of”. Divide by the denominator: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 5 = 15. So 34 of 20 = 15.

items.q: Find 38 of 32.

items.q: 29 × 54 = ?

items.q: Find 58 of 64.

items.q: 512 × 60 = ?

items.q: 63 × 79 = ?
items.e: × means “of”. Divide by the denominator: 63 ÷ 9 = 7 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 7 × 7 = 49. So 79 of 63 = 49.

items.q: Which calculation gives the same answer as 34 × 20?
items.e: 34 × 20 means 34 of 20: divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator. 20 ÷ 4 × 3 = 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: ?5 of 30 = 18. What is the missing numerator?
items.e: One fifth of 30 is 30 ÷ 5 = 6. 18 ÷ 6 = 3, so 18 is 3 fifths: 35 of 30 = 18. The missing numerator is 3.

items.q: Which is greater: 23 of 15 or 35 of 20?
items.e: 23 of 15: 15 ÷ 3 = 5, 5 × 2 = 10. 35 of 20: 20 ÷ 5 = 4, 4 × 3 = 12. 12 is greater than 10, so 35 of 20 is greater.

sets.title: Multiply mixed numbers by whole numbers

items.q: Each row shows 2 14. There are 3 rows. What is 2 14 × 3?
items.e: Count the whole bars: 3 × 2 = 6. Count the shaded parts in the last column: 3 × 1 = 3 quarters. Partition 2 14 into 2 and 14. Multiply each part by 3: 2 × 3 = 6 and 14 × 3 = 34. Add: 6 + 34 = 6 34.

items.q: Each row shows 1 25. There are 2 rows. What is 1 25 × 2?
items.e: Count the whole bars: 2 × 1 = 2. Count the shaded parts in the last column: 2 × 2 = 4 fifths. Partition 1 25 into 1 and 25. Multiply each part by 2: 1 × 2 = 2 and 25 × 2 = 45. Add: 2 + 45 = 2 45.

items.q: Each row shows 1 15. There are 4 rows. What is 1 15 × 4?
items.e: Count the whole bars: 4 × 1 = 4. Count the shaded parts in the last column: 4 × 1 = 4 fifths. Partition 1 15 into 1 and 15. Multiply each part by 4: 1 × 4 = 4 and 15 × 4 = 45. Add: 4 + 45 = 4 45.

items.q: Each row shows 2 13. There are 2 rows. What is 2 13 × 2?
items.e: Count the whole bars: 2 × 2 = 4. Count the shaded parts in the last column: 2 × 1 = 2 thirds. Partition 2 13 into 2 and 13. Multiply each part by 2: 2 × 2 = 4 and 13 × 2 = 23. Add: 4 + 23 = 4 23.

items.q: 1 27 × 3 = ?
items.e: Partition 1 27 into 1 and 27. Multiply each part by 3: 1 × 3 = 3 and 27 × 3 = 67. Add: 3 + 67 = 3 67.

items.q: 2 × 3 25 = ?
items.e: Partition 3 25 into 3 and 25. Multiply each part by 2: 3 × 2 = 6 and 25 × 2 = 45. Add: 6 + 45 = 6 45.

items.q: 2 15 × 4 = ?
items.e: Partition 2 15 into 2 and 15. Multiply each part by 4: 2 × 4 = 8 and 15 × 4 = 45. Add: 8 + 45 = 8 45.

items.q: 3 × 4 27 = ?
items.e: Partition 4 27 into 4 and 27. Multiply each part by 3: 4 × 3 = 12 and 27 × 3 = 67. Add: 12 + 67 = 12 67.

items.q: 5 49 × 2 = ?
items.e: Partition 5 49 into 5 and 49. Multiply each part by 2: 5 × 2 = 10 and 49 × 2 = 89. Add: 10 + 89 = 10 89.

items.q: 5 × 1 16 = ?
items.e: Partition 1 16 into 1 and 16. Multiply each part by 5: 1 × 5 = 5 and 16 × 5 = 56. Add: 5 + 56 = 5 56.

items.q: 3 14 × 3 = ?
items.e: Partition 3 14 into 3 and 14. Multiply each part by 3: 3 × 3 = 9 and 14 × 3 = 34. Add: 9 + 34 = 9 34.

items.q: 2 × 7 13 = ?
items.e: Partition 7 13 into 7 and 13. Multiply each part by 2: 7 × 2 = 14 and 13 × 2 = 23. Add: 14 + 23 = 14 23.

items.q: Isla says 2 14 × 3 = 6 14. What mistake did she make?
c: She multiplied only the whole number.
items.e: Both parts must be multiplied by 3: 2 × 3 = 6 and 14 × 3 = 34. So 2 14 × 3 = 6 34, not 6 14.

items.q: Change 1 23 to an improper fraction, then multiply by 4. What is 1 23 × 4?
items.e: 1 23 = 53 (1 × 3 + 2 = 5). 53 × 4 = 203. 20 ÷ 3 = 6 remainder 2, so the answer is 6 23.

items.q: Each bottle holds 34 of a litre of water. How much water is in 6 bottles?
items.e: 6 × 34. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 6 × 3 = 18, so the answer is 184. 18 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 2, so 184 = 4 24 = 4 12 litres.

items.q: A loaf of bread needs 25 kg of flour. How much flour is needed for 4 loaves?
items.e: 4 × 25. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 4 × 2 = 8, so the answer is 85. 8 ÷ 5 = 1 remainder 3, so 85 = 1 35 kg.

items.q: Each bow uses 35 m of ribbon. Jack makes 7 bows. How much ribbon does he use?
items.e: 7 × 35. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 7 × 3 = 21, so the answer is 215. 21 ÷ 5 = 4 remainder 1, so 215 = 4 15 m.

items.q: Each lesson lasts 34 of an hour. How many hours are 5 lessons?
items.e: 5 × 34. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 5 × 3 = 15, so the answer is 154. 15 ÷ 4 = 3 remainder 3, so 154 = 3 34 hours.

items.q: Each pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Each of 6 pupils eats 38 of a pizza. How much pizza do they eat altogether?
items.e: 6 × 38. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 6 × 3 = 18, so the answer is 188. 18 ÷ 8 = 2 remainder 2, so 188 = 2 28 = 2 14 pizzas.

items.q: Leo reads for 23 of an hour every night. How many hours does he read in 7 nights?
items.e: 7 × 23. Multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator: 7 × 2 = 14, so the answer is 143. 14 ÷ 3 = 4 remainder 2, so 143 = 4 23 hours.

items.q: There are 32 pupils in a Year 5 class. 38 of them have school dinners. How many pupils have school dinners?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 32 ÷ 8 = 4 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 4 = 12. So 38 of 32 = 12 pupils.

items.q: A coat costs £60. In a sale, it costs 34 of the price. What is the sale price?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: £60 ÷ 4 = £15 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × £15 = £45. So 34 of £60 = £45.

items.q: A football match lasts 90 minutes. 23 of the match has been played. How many minutes is that?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 90 ÷ 3 = 30 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 30 = 60. So 23 of 90 = 60 minutes.

items.q: Alfie needs £32 for a school trip. He has saved 58 of it. How much has he saved?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: £32 ÷ 8 = £4 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 5 × £4 = £20. So 58 of £32 = £20.

items.q: A box has 45 packets of crisps. 25 of the packets are cheese and onion. How many packets are cheese and onion?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 45 ÷ 5 = 9 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 9 = 18. So 25 of 45 = 18 packets.

items.q: A bag of potatoes weighs 2 12 kg. The school cook buys 3 bags. How much do they weigh altogether?
items.e: Partition 2 12 into 2 and 12. Multiply each part by 3: 2 × 3 = 6 and 12 × 3 = 32 = 1 12. Add: 6 + 1 12 = 7 12 kg.

items.q: A jug holds 1 34 litres of squash. How much squash is in 4 full jugs?
items.e: Partition 1 34 into 1 and 34. Multiply each part by 4: 1 × 4 = 4 and 34 × 4 = 124 = 3. Add: 4 + 3 = 7 litres.

items.q: A plank is 1 25 m long. Grace puts 3 planks end to end. How long is the row of planks?
items.e: Partition 1 25 into 1 and 25. Multiply each part by 3: 1 × 3 = 3 and 25 × 3 = 65 = 1 15. Add: 3 + 1 15 = 4 15 m.

items.q: A sunflower grows 2 13 cm each day. How much does it grow in 6 days?
items.e: Partition 2 13 into 2 and 13. Multiply each part by 6: 2 × 6 = 12 and 13 × 6 = 63 = 2. Add: 12 + 2 = 14 cm.

items.q: A bucket holds 4 12 litres of water. How much water is in 3 full buckets?
items.e: Partition 4 12 into 4 and 12. Multiply each part by 3: 4 × 3 = 12 and 12 × 3 = 32 = 1 12. Add: 12 + 1 12 = 13 12 litres.

items.q: A lorry carries 3 34 tonnes of sand on each trip. How much sand does it carry in 4 trips?
items.e: Partition 3 34 into 3 and 34. Multiply each part by 4: 3 × 4 = 12 and 34 × 4 = 124 = 3. Add: 12 + 3 = 15 tonnes.

items.q: Zara walks 23 km to school and 23 km home every school day. How far does she walk in 5 school days?
items.e: Each day she walks there and back: 2 × 23 = 43 km. In 5 days: 5 × 43 = 203 km. 20 ÷ 3 = 6 remainder 2, so she walks 6 23 km.

items.q: Harry has 4 m of string. He cuts 5 pieces, each 23 m long. How much string is left?
items.e: First find the string used: 5 × 23 = 103 m = 3 13 m. Then subtract: 4 − 3 13 = 23 m.

items.q: Mohammed has 4 bottles that each hold 34 litre. Noah has 3 bottles that each hold 1 14 litres. Who has more?
items.e: Mohammed: 4 × 34 = 124 = 3 litres. Noah: 3 × 1 14 = 3 + 34 = 3 34 litres. 3 34 litres is more, so Noah has more.
